correctness.rationale: For p,q≥2 and 1≤t<min(p,q), unmatched universal vertices on each bipartite side force every side color-class cardinality odd. Each matched endpoint must be a within-side singleton: otherwise its deleted partner sees a positive even count. Properness permits a color to span both sides only for the endpoints of one missing matched edge. Such singleton merges are mutually independent and sufficient for the strong-odd neighborhood parity condition. Thus side-unmatched vertices partition into odd blocks independently, and choosing j merges among t missing pairs creates 2t+k+ℓ−j global classes. Injective naming yields Φ(Q)=Σ Sodd(p−t,k)Sodd(q−t,ℓ)binom(t,j)(Q)_{2t+k+ℓ−j}; no double counting. Minimal k,ℓ are ε(u)=1 if u odd or 2 if even, with c(u)=1 or 2^(u−2), and all t merges are compulsory at optimum. The small m=r=1 boundary and zero palette are covered. Independent fresh restricted-growth partition enumeration against original adjacency and neighborhood definition confirmed four parameter triples including (2,2,1), (3,3,1), (3,4,2), (4,4,1), and coefficients.
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate, but do not establish, the universal claim.
